And with his chain, from Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar, Maysar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Zayd, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Qatadah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is meant by His saying ﴿which of you is best in deed﴾?" He said: "It means: which of you is best in intellect."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "The most complete of you in intellect and the most fearful of Allah among you, and the best of you in looking at what Allah has commanded and forbidden, even if he is the least of you in voluntary acts." [350] [[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 12/9.]] [351] [[Tafsir Majma al-Bayan: 10/69.]]

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl informed us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya al-Qurashi related to us: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Suqayq related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Ash'ath, from Fudayl ibn Iyad, regarding His saying ﴿that He may test you, which of you is best in deed﴾, that he said: "Its sincerity and its correctness." I said: "What is its sincerity and what is its correctness?" He said: "Indeed, if a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it is not accepted, until it is both sincere and correct. Sincere means it is for Allah, and correct means it is according to the sunnah (the prophetic way)."

Al-Hasan said: It means: which of you is most ascetic toward this world in asceticism, and most abandoning of it in abandonment.

Sahl said: Which of you is best in trust in Allah.

Al-Farra' said: The word al-balwa (test) is not put in the nominative with ayyukum (which of you), because between ayyu (which) and the test there is an implied element. It is like when one says in speech: "We tested you to see which of you is more obedient." Similarly, His saying ﴿Ask them which of them will stand surety for that﴾, meaning: ask them and consider which of them.

So ayyu is in the nominative as the subject of the sentence, and aḥsanu (best) is its predicate.

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Forgiving, who created seven heavens in layers﴾: tibaqan means one layer upon another, one above another. It is said: "atbaqtu al-shay'" when one places part of a thing above another.

Aban ibn Taghlib said: I heard some Bedouins blame a man, and one said: "His evil is layered, and his good is not lasting."

Sibawayh said: tibaqan is in the accusative because it is a second object.

﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no disproportion﴾. Yahya ibn Thabit, al-A'mash, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read: min tafawwut, without an alif, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and the reading of Abd Allah and his companions.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq informed us: Makki ibn Abdan informed us: Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, that he used to read: min tafawwut.

Al-A'mash said: I mentioned this to Abu Razin, and he said: "I heard it from Abd Allah before, and I accepted and took it."

The others read tafawut, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. Both are dialects, like al-ta'ahhud and al-ta'aahud, al-tahammul and al-tahamul, al-tatahhur and al-tatahhur. The meaning is: you see in the creation of the Most Merciful no crookedness, no discrepancy, no contradiction, no divergence; rather it is even and straight. Its root is from al-fawt, which is that some parts pass beyond others due to their lack of evenness. This is shown by the saying of Ibn Abbas: "min tafarruq" (from divergence). [[See Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 8/58.]]

﴿Then return﴾: al-Farra' said: He said "then return" without any previously mentioned verb to which the return refers, because the sense of the speech is: "Look, then return the gaze."

﴿Do you see any flaw﴾: futur means cracks, fissures, and holes.

Al-Dahhak: discrepancy and breaks. Ata: a defect. Ibn Kaysan: separation. Al-Qurazi: wounds. Abu Ubaydah: rifts. [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/5-6, and Fath al-Qadir: 5/259.]] Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud said:

"I split the heart, then scattered into it
your love, so it was joined and the cracks closed."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 4/303.]]

Another said:

"It penetrated where no drink reached,
nor intoxication, nor joy reached."

Another said:

"He built you a sky without pillars,
and adorned it, and there is no flaw in it."
[[The verses are in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/209.]]

﴿Then return the gaze﴾: repeat the looking, and reexamine, ﴿twice﴾: two times. ﴿It will return to you, dazzled﴾: humbled, abased, distanced, ﴿while it is weary﴾: meaning exhausted, worn out, not having attained what it sought. A poet said:

"I looked at her at al-Muhassab in Mina,
then my gaze came back to me, and it was weary."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/210.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us: al-Hasan ibn Alawayh related to us: Isma'il ibn Isa related to us: al-Musayyab related to us: Ibrahim al-Bakri related to us, from Salih ibn Jabbar, from Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from his father. Al-Musayyab said: Abu Ja'far also related to us, from al-Rabi', from Ka'b, the two of them saying: The lowest heaven is a surging, restrained wave; the second is white marble; the third is iron; the fourth is brass, and Nahhas said: "and the fifth is silver; the sixth is gold; and the seventh is a red ruby. Between the seventh heaven and the seven veils are deserts of light. The name of the keeper of the veils is 'Fanṭaṭrus'."

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾: that is, the stars; its singular is miṣbāḥ, which is a lamp.

﴿And We made them missiles against the devils﴾, a target for them when they steal hearing, ﴿and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾ in the Hereafter, beyond what We made for them in this world of shooting stars. ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord, also﴾ is the punishment of Hell, ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾. ﴿When they are cast into it, they hear from it a roaring, a sound like the braying of a donkey, ﴿while it boils﴾, surging and seething with them as a cauldron seethes.

Mujahid said: It surges with them as a little grain surges in much water.

﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾: its parts split from one another out of rage against its people, and for the vengeance of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Every time a company is cast into it﴾, a group of people, ﴿its keepers ask them: Did no warner come to you?﴾, a messenger in the world. ﴿They say: Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied and said to the messengers: Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in a great error.﴾

Meccan. It has thirty verses, three hundred and thirty words, and one thousand three hundred and twenty letters.

Abu Muhammad al-Makhladi related to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: al-Abbas ibn Abd Allah al-Tirmidhi related to us: Hafs ibn Umar related to us: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I wish that ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾ were in the heart of every believer." [348]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi informed me: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us: Abu Yahya al-Bazzar related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us: Abu Dawud related to us: Imran related to us, from Qatadah, from Abbas al-Jushami, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a surah of the Book of Allah, which is only thirty verses, interceded for a man and brought him out of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and admitted him into Paradise. It is the surah of ﴿Tabaraka﴾." [349] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/205.]]

Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi Ishaq al-Muzakki and Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Fadl al-Adl informed us, both saying: Ismail ibn Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Saffar related to us: Sadan ibn Nasr related to us: Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Khalil ibn Murrah, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, who narrated it from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "When the deceased is placed in his grave, he is approached from the direction of his feet, and it is said: 'You have no way over him, for he used to stand (in prayer) with the Surah of the Sovereignty (al-Mulk).' Then he is approached from the direction of his head, and his tongue says: 'You have no way over me, for he used to recite me, the Surah of the Sovereignty.'" Then he said: "It is the one that prevents the punishment of the grave. In the Torah it is called the Surah of the Sovereignty. Whoever recites it in a night has gained much and good."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life﴾

He mentioned death before life because it is closer to subjugation (al-qahr), just as He mentioned daughters before sons in His saying: ﴿He bestows female offspring upon whom He wills, and He bestows males upon whom He wills﴾.

Qatadah said: Allah humbled the son of Adam through death, made this world a place of life and a place of perishing, and made the Hereafter a place of recompense and permanence. It was also said: He mentioned it first because it is earlier, since things at their beginning were in the state of lifelessness, such as the drop of semen and the dust and the like, and then life came upon them.

Ibn Abbas said: Death was created in the form of a white-spotted ram, which does not pass by anything, nor does anything smell its scent, except that it dies. And life was created in the form of a dappled mare, which Gabriel and the prophets (peace be upon them) used to ride. Its stride is as far as the eye can see; it is above the donkey and below the mule. It does not pass by anything nor tread upon anything, and nothing smells its scent except that it lives. It is the one from whose hoofprint al-Samiri took a handful and cast it upon the calf, and it came alive.

﴿That He may test you, which of you is best in deed﴾: in the period between life and death.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Barzah related to us: al-Harith ibn Usamah related to us: Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar related to us: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad al-Abdi related to us, from Kulayb ibn Wa'il, from Ibn Umar, that the Prophet (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi) recited ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾ until he reached His saying ﴿which of you is best in deed﴾. Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us: al-Hasan ibn Alawayh related to us: Isma'il ibn Isa related to us: al-Musayyab related to us: Ibrahim al-Bakri related to us, from Salih ibn Jabbar, from Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from his father. Al-Musayyab said: Abu Ja'far also related to us, from al-Rabi', from Ka'b, the two of them saying: The lowest heaven is a surging, restrained wave; the second is white marble; the third is iron; the fourth is brass, and Nahhas said: "and the fifth is silver; the sixth is gold; and the seventh is a red ruby. Between the seventh heaven and the seven veils are deserts of light. The name of the keeper of the veils is 'Fanṭaṭrus'."

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾: that is, the stars; its singular is miṣbāḥ, which is a lamp.

﴿And We made them missiles against the devils﴾, a target for them when they steal hearing, ﴿and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾ in the Hereafter, beyond what We made for them in this world of shooting stars. ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord, also﴾ is the punishment of Hell, ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾. ﴿When they are cast into it, they hear from it a roaring, a sound like the braying of a donkey, ﴿while it boils﴾, surging and seething with them as a cauldron seethes.

Mujahid said: It surges with them as a little grain surges in much water.

﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾: its parts split from one another out of rage against its people, and for the vengeance of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Every time a company is cast into it﴾, a group of people, ﴿its keepers ask them: Did no warner come to you?﴾, a messenger in the world. ﴿They say: Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied and said to the messengers: Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in a great error.﴾

They said, while in the Fire: "Had we listened to the warnings of the messengers and what they brought to us, or had we used our reason regarding them..." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Had we listened to guidance, or understood it, and acted upon it."

﴿They will say: "Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the blaze."﴾ So they will confess their sin. ﴿Away with them, the companions of the blaze!﴾ Fasuhqan means "far away," "distance." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is a valley in Hell. Abu Ja'far and al-Kisa'i, in both transmissions of al-Duri and Qutayba, transmitted a difference of reading regarding it, while the others verified it. Both forms are dialectal variants, like al-Ru'b and al-Ru'b (terror), and al-Suht and al-Suht (illicit gain).

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa informed us, from Isra'il, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A man will be dragged toward the Fire, and it will shrink and contract, drawing its parts together. Then the Merciful will say to it, 'What is the matter with you?' It will say, 'He used to seek refuge from me,' and He will say, 'Release My servant.' Another man will be dragged toward the Fire, and he will say, 'O Lord, this was not the opinion you had of Yourself!' He will say, 'And what was your opinion?' He will say, 'My opinion was that Your mercy would encompass me.' So He will say, 'Release My servant.' Another man will be dragged toward the Fire, and the Fire will groan toward him with a groan like that of a mule toward barley, then it will exhale a breath, and no one will remain but that he is afraid."

﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, for them is forgiveness and a great reward. And whether you keep your speech secret or declare it aloud, He is Knower of what is in the breasts. Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists who would disparage the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Gabriel would inform him of what they said and of their insults. Some of them would say to others: "Keep your speech secret, lest the god of Muhammad hear it."

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: if you wish, you may take "man" in His words ﴿man khalaq﴾ as a name for the Creator, so the meaning becomes: "Should the Creator not know what is in the breasts, He who is the Subtle, the All-Aware?" And if you wish, you may take it as a noun, so the meaning becomes: "Should Allah not know His creation?"

Al-Fanjawi informed us: Musa ibn al-Hasan ibn Alawiyya informed us: Isa ibn Isma'il ibn Isa ibn al-Musayyib informed us, who said: "A man was standing at night among many trees, and the wind was rustling, and a thought came to the man, so he said: 'Does God know what falls of these leaves?' Then he was called from behind him: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?!﴾"

Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated from Zurayn, from Ibn Abi Asma', that a man entered a thicket and said: "If I were alone here for disobedience, who would see me?" He said: "He heard a voice that filled what was between the two lava-fields of the thicket: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?!﴾"

﴿He it is who made the earth subservient to you, tractable, easy, subjected, not resisting, so walk in its broad tracts (manakibiha).﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Qatada said: in its mountains. Al-Dahhak: in its hills. Mujahid: its paths and passes. Al-Kalbi said: its edges. Al-Farra': in its sides. Muqatil: its regions. Al-Hasan: its plains, wherever you wish, for He has made it tractable for you, not resisting. The root of al-mankib is the side, and from it comes "the shoulder of a man," and "al-rih al-nakkab" (a wind blowing from one side), and "tanakkaba fulan" (he deviated).

﴿And eat of His provision, and unto Him is the resurrection.﴾

﴿Do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you feel secure from the punishment of He who is in the heaven, should you disobey Him?"

It has been said: the meaning of ﴿man fi al-sama'﴾ is His power, His authority, His throne, and His dominion. It has also been said: He said ﴿man fi al-sama'﴾ because they used to acknowledge that He is the God of the heaven, while claiming that the idols are gods of the earth. They would call upon Allah from the direction of the heaven and await the descent of His command, with mercy or with severity, from it.

The verifying scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) said: [in the manuscript: al-mutahaqqiqun] The meaning of His words ﴿fi al-sama'﴾ is "above the heaven," like His words ﴿So travel in the earth﴾ [Q 9:2], meaning above it, not by contact or confinement, but by domination and governance.

It has also been said: its meaning is "upon the heaven," like His words ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Q 20:71]. Its meaning is that He is its owner, its governor, and its overseer, just as one says, "So-and-so is over Iraq and the Hijaz," and "So-and-so is over Khurasan and Sijistan," meaning that he is its governor and its commander.

Know that the verses and sound reports on this subject are numerous, and all of them point to elevation. None rejects them except an atheist who denies or an ignorant obstinate person. Their intended meaning, Allah knows best, is to venerate Him, glorify Him, and declare Him free from being low or beneath, and to describe Him with elevation and greatness, without describing Him as having places, directions, limits, or states, for these are the attributes of bodies and signs of createdness. Allah the Exalted existed when there was no place, and He created places without needing them, and He is as He has always been. Do you not see that people raise their hands in supplication toward the heaven, although His knowledge, power, and dominion encompass the earth and everything else just as they encompass the heaven? Yet the heaven is the place of descent of revelation, the place from which rain descends, the seat of holiness, and the source of the purified, the near angels, and to it the deeds of His servants are raised, and above it is His throne and His paradise. And success is from Allah.

﴿Lest He cause the earth to swallow you, and behold, it quakes.﴾ Al-Hasan said: it shakes with its inhabitants. Al-Dahhak said: it spins with them while they are at its bottom. Ibn Kaysan said: it plunges them down.

﴿Or do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven, that He might send upon you a violent wind with stones, as He did to the people of Lut and the companions of the Elephant? Then you will know how My warning was.﴾ Meaning: how My warning of punishment was.

﴿And those before them had already denied, so how was My rejection?﴾ Meaning: how My rejection (nakir) was. Some reciters affirmed the yā' in these letters and their responses, in accordance with the original form, while others omitted it, following the written form.

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Merciful. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.﴾ Spreading their wings means extending them while flying, and folding them means gathering them after spreading. "Ma yumsikuhunna" means: what holds them, i.e., restrains them, while they fold and spread their wings, from falling.

﴿Who is this that could be a host for you, to help you apart from the Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: [who is this that could be] a protection for you. [He could] help you, so that He would repel from you what He intends for you.

﴿Who is this that could provide for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ "But they persisted in insolence (utuww)," in error, "and aversion (nufur)," moving away from the truth.

﴿Is one who walks prone upon his face more rightly guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ The first is the one who walks prone upon his face, with his head fallen into error and ignorance, blind of heart and eye, not seeing right or left, and this is the disbeliever. Qatada said: this is the disbeliever who hastened upon the disobedience of Allah in this world, so Allah will gather him on the Day of Resurrection upon his face. "One who walks upright on a straight path" is the believer.

His words ﴿mukiban ala wajhihi﴾ are an unusual expression, because most of the language in transitive and intransitive usage has the form of af'ala with yufa'ilu. This is the reverse: one says "kubbtu fulanan ala wajhihi fa-akabba," meaning "I turned so-and-so upon his face, and he fell prone." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾ [Q 27:90].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do people get thrown upon their faces into the Fire for anything other than the harvest of their tongues?"

Its parallel in speech is the saying: "The wind dispersed the clouds, and they dispersed (aqsha'at)," and "I gave him the good news of a child, and he received good news (absha)." It has also been said: "mukiban" is because it is an act not yet fully realized. Do you not see that people raise their hands in supplication toward the heaven, although His knowledge, power, and dominion encompass the earth and everything else just as they encompass the heaven? Yet the heaven is the place of descent of revelation, the place from which rain descends, the seat of holiness, and the source of the purified, the near angels, and to it the deeds of His servants are raised, and above it is His throne and His paradise. And success is from Allah.

﴿Lest He cause the earth to swallow you, and behold, it quakes.﴾ Al-Hasan said: it shakes with its inhabitants. Al-Dahhak said: it spins with them while they are at its bottom. Ibn Kaysan said: it plunges them down.

Prone upon his two tusks, his mane shaking,
over the back of a stripe-marked, bewildered lion.

The common reading is ﴿tadda'un﴾ with the doubled dal, of the form "yaftaʻilun" from "du'a'" (calling). According to most scholars, this means they wish for it and seek consolation. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, and the view of Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya and Ibn Kaysan.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: this refers to the water of Zamzam, and the well of Maymun al-Hadrami, which is an ancient well of the 'Ad.

They said, while in the Fire: "Had we listened to the warnings of the messengers and what they brought to us, or had we used our reason regarding them..." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Had we listened to guidance, or understood it, and acted upon it."

﴿They will say: "Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the blaze."﴾ So they will confess their sin. ﴿Away with them, the companions of the blaze!﴾ Fasuhqan means "far away," "distance." Both forms are dialectal variants, like al-Ru'b and al-Ru'b (terror), and al-Suht and al-Suht (illicit gain).

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa informed us, from Isra'il, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A man will be dragged toward the Fire, and it will shrink and contract, drawing its parts together. Then the Merciful will say to it, 'What is the matter with you?' It will say, 'He used to seek refuge from me,' and He will say, 'Release My servant.' Another man will be dragged toward the Fire, and he will say, 'O Lord, this was not the opinion you had of Yourself!' He will say, 'And what was your opinion?' He will say, 'My opinion was that Your mercy would encompass me.' So He will say, 'Release My servant.' Another man will be dragged toward the Fire, and the Fire will groan toward him with a groan like that of a mule toward barley, then it will exhale a breath, and no one will remain but that he is afraid."

﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, for them is forgiveness and a great reward. And whether you keep your speech secret or declare it aloud, He is Knower of what is in the breasts. Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists who would disparage the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Gabriel would inform him of what they said and of their insults. Some of them would say to others: "Keep your speech secret, lest the god of Muhammad hear it."

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: if you wish, you may take "man" in His words ﴿man khalaq﴾ as a name for the Creator, so the meaning becomes: "Should the Creator not know what is in the breasts, He who is the Subtle, the All-Aware?" And if you wish, you may take it as a noun, so the meaning becomes: "Should Allah not know His creation?"

Al-Fanjawi informed us: Musa ibn al-Hasan ibn Alawiyya informed us: Isa ibn Isma'il ibn Isa ibn al-Musayyib informed us, who said: "A man was standing at night among many trees, and the wind was rustling, and a thought came to the man, so he said: 'Does God know what falls of these leaves?' Then he was called from behind him: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?!﴾"

Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated from Zurayn, from Ibn Abi Asma', that a man entered a thicket and said: "If I were alone here for disobedience, who would see me?" He said: "He heard a voice that filled what was between the two lava-fields of the thicket: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?!﴾"

﴿He it is who made the earth subservient to you, tractable, easy, subjected, not resisting, so walk in its broad tracts (manakibiha).﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Qatada said: in its mountains. Al-Dahhak: in its hills. Mujahid: its paths and passes. Al-Kalbi said: its edges. Al-Farra': in its sides. Muqatil: its regions. Al-Hasan: its plains, wherever you wish, for He has made it tractable for you, not resisting. The root of al-mankib is the side, and from it comes "the shoulder of a man," and "al-rih al-nakkab" (a wind blowing from one side), and "tanakkaba fulan" (he deviated).

﴿And eat of His provision, and unto Him is the resurrection.﴾

﴿Do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you feel secure from the punishment of He who is in the heaven, should you disobey Him?"

It has been said: the meaning of ﴿man fi al-sama'﴾ is His power, His authority, His throne, and His dominion. It has also been said: He said ﴿man fi al-sama'﴾ because they used to acknowledge that He is the God of the heaven, while claiming that the idols are gods of the earth. They would call upon Allah from the direction of the heaven and await the descent of His command, with mercy or with severity, from it.

The verifying scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) said: [in the manuscript: al-mutahaqqiqun] The meaning of His words ﴿fi al-sama'﴾ is "above the heaven," like His words ﴿So travel in the earth﴾ [Q 9:2], meaning above it, not by contact or confinement, but by domination and governance.

It has also been said: its meaning is "upon the heaven," like His words ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Q 20:71]. Its meaning is that He is its owner, its governor, and its overseer, just as one says, "So-and-so is over Iraq and the Hijaz," and "So-and-so is over Khurasan and Sijistan," meaning that he is its governor and its commander.

Know that the verses and sound reports on this subject are numerous, and all of them point to elevation. None rejects them except an atheist who denies or an ignorant obstinate person. Their intended meaning, Allah knows best, is to venerate Him, glorify Him, and declare Him free from being low or beneath, and to describe Him with elevation and greatness, without describing Him as having places, directions, limits, or states, for these are the attributes of bodies and signs of createdness. Do you not see that people raise their hands in supplication toward the heaven, although His knowledge, power, and dominion encompass the earth and everything else just as they encompass the heaven? Yet the heaven is the place of descent of revelation, the place from which rain descends, the seat of holiness, and the source of the purified, the near angels, and to it the deeds of His servants are raised, and above it is His throne and His paradise. And success is from Allah.

﴿Lest He cause the earth to swallow you, and behold, it quakes.﴾ Al-Hasan said: it shakes with its inhabitants. Al-Dahhak said: it spins with them while they are at its bottom. Ibn Kaysan said: it plunges them down.

Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.﴾ Spreading their wings means extending them while flying, and folding them means gathering them after spreading. "Ma yumsikuhunna" means: what holds them, i.e., restrains them, while they fold and spread their wings, from falling.

﴿Who is this that could be a host for you, to help you apart from the Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: [who is this that could be] a protection for you. [He could] help you, so that He would repel from you what He intends for you.

Prone upon his two tusks, his mane shaking,
over the back of a stripe-marked, bewildered lion.

He will say, 'My opinion was that Your mercy would encompass me.' So He will say, 'Release My servant.' Another man will be dragged toward the Fire, and the Fire will groan toward him with a groan like that of a mule toward barley, then it will exhale a breath, and no one will remain but that he is afraid."

﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, for them is forgiveness and a great reward. And whether you keep your speech secret or declare it aloud, He is Knower of what is in the breasts. Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists who would disparage the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Gabriel would inform him of what they said and of their insults. Some of them would say to others: "Keep your speech secret, lest the god of Muhammad hear it."

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: if you wish, you may take "man" in His words ﴿man khalaq﴾ as a name for the Creator, so the meaning becomes: "Should the Creator not know what is in the breasts, He who is the Subtle, the All-Aware?" And if you wish, you may take it as a noun, so the meaning becomes: "Should Allah not know His creation?"

Al-Fanjawi informed us: Musa ibn al-Hasan ibn Alawiyya informed us: Isa ibn Isma'il ibn Isa ibn al-Musayyib informed us, who said: "A man was standing at night among many trees, and the wind was rustling, and a thought came to the man, so he said: 'Does God know what falls of these leaves?' Then he was called from behind him: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?!﴾"

Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated from Zurayn, from Ibn Abi Asma', that a man entered a thicket and said: "If I were alone here for disobedience, who would see me?" He said: "He heard a voice that filled what was between the two lava-fields of the thicket: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?!﴾"

﴿He it is who made the earth subservient to you, tractable, easy, subjected, not resisting, so walk in its broad tracts (manakibiha).﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Qatada said: in its mountains. Al-Dahhak: in its hills. Mujahid: its paths and passes. Al-Kalbi said: its edges. Al-Farra': in its sides. Muqatil: its regions. Al-Hasan: its plains, wherever you wish, for He has made it tractable for you, not resisting. The root of al-mankib is the side, and from it comes "the shoulder of a man," and "al-rih al-nakkab" (a wind blowing from one side), and "tanakkaba fulan" (he deviated).

﴿And eat of His provision, and unto Him is the resurrection.﴾

﴿Do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you feel secure from the punishment of He who is in the heaven, should you disobey Him?"

It has been said: the meaning of ﴿man fi al-sama'﴾ is His power, His authority, His throne, and His dominion. It has also been said: He said ﴿man fi al-sama'﴾ because they used to acknowledge that He is the God of the heaven, while claiming that the idols are gods of the earth. They would call upon Allah from the direction of the heaven and await the descent of His command, with mercy or with severity, from it.

The verifying scholars (al-muhaqqiqun) said: [in the manuscript: al-mutahaqqiqun] The meaning of His words ﴿fi al-sama'﴾ is "above the heaven," like His words ﴿So travel in the earth﴾ [Q 9:2], meaning above it, not by contact or confinement, but by domination and governance.

It has also been said: its meaning is "upon the heaven," like His words ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Q 20:71]. Its meaning is that He is its owner, its governor, and its overseer, just as one says, "So-and-so is over Iraq and the Hijaz," and "So-and-so is over Khurasan and Sijistan," meaning that he is its governor and its commander.

Know that the verses and sound reports on this subject are numerous, and all of them point to elevation. None rejects them except an atheist who denies or an ignorant obstinate person. Their intended meaning, Allah knows best, is to venerate Him, glorify Him, and declare Him free from being low or beneath, and to describe Him with elevation and greatness, without describing Him as having places, directions, limits, or states, for these are the attributes of bodies and signs of createdness. Allah the Exalted existed when there was no place, and He created places without needing them, and He is as He has always been. Do you not see that people raise their hands in supplication toward the heaven, although His knowledge, power, and dominion encompass the earth and everything else just as they encompass the heaven? Yet the heaven is the place of descent of revelation, the place from which rain descends, the seat of holiness, and the source of the purified, the near angels, and to it the deeds of His servants are raised, and above it is His throne and His paradise. And success is from Allah.

﴿Lest He cause the earth to swallow you, and behold, it quakes.﴾ Al-Hasan said: it shakes with its inhabitants. Al-Dahhak said: it spins with them while they are at its bottom. Ibn Kaysan said: it plunges them down.

﴿Or do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven, that He might send upon you a violent wind with stones, as He did to the people of Lut and the companions of the Elephant? Then you will know how My warning was.﴾ Meaning: how My warning of punishment was.

﴿And those before them had already denied, so how was My rejection?﴾ Meaning: how My rejection (nakir) was. Some reciters affirmed the yā' in these letters and their responses, in accordance with the original form, while others omitted it, following the written form.

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Merciful. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.﴾ Spreading their wings means extending them while flying, and folding them means gathering them after spreading. "Ma yumsikuhunna" means: what holds them, i.e., restrains them, while they fold and spread their wings, from falling.

﴿Who is this that could be a host for you, to help you apart from the Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: [who is this that could be] a protection for you. [He could] help you, so that He would repel from you what He intends for you.

﴿Who is this that could provide for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ "But they persisted in insolence (utuww)," in error, "and aversion (nufur)," moving away from the truth.

﴿Is one who walks prone upon his face more rightly guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ The first is the one who walks prone upon his face, with his head fallen into error and ignorance, blind of heart and eye, not seeing right or left, and this is the disbeliever. Qatada said: this is the disbeliever who hastened upon the disobedience of Allah in this world, so Allah will gather him on the Day of Resurrection upon his face. "One who walks upright on a straight path" is the believer.

His words ﴿mukiban ala wajhihi﴾ are an unusual expression, because most of the language in transitive and intransitive usage has the form of af'ala with yufa'ilu. This is the reverse: one says "kubbtu fulanan ala wajhihi fa-akabba," meaning "I turned so-and-so upon his face, and he fell prone." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾ [Q 27:90].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do people get thrown upon their faces into the Fire for anything other than the harvest of their tongues?"

Its parallel in speech is the saying: "The wind dispersed the clouds, and they dispersed (aqsha'at)," and "I gave him the good news of a child, and he received good news (absha)." It has also been said: "mukiban" is because it is an act not yet fully realized. In Tafsir al-Tabari there is an addition: when it is not realized, they introduce the alif, so they say: "Akabba fulan ala wajhihi, fa-huwa mukibb," and from it is the verse of al-A'sha: [The poem, as it stands:]

Prone upon his two tusks, his mane shaking,
over the back of a stripe-marked, bewildered lion.

﴿Say: He it is who produced you and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little are you grateful.﴾ ﴿Say: He it is who multiplied you upon the earth, and unto Him you will be gathered.﴾

﴿And they say: When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ ﴿Say: The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.﴾

﴿But when they see it﴾, meaning the punishment in the Hereafter according to most exegetes, while Mujahid said: it means the punishment at Badr, ﴿approaching﴾, meaning near. It is a noun of quality functioning as a verbal noun, in which the masculine and feminine, singular and dual and plural, are alike.

﴿Their faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed﴾, meaning: disgraced, and their faces will be blackened and covered with gloom and estrangement. People say: "sawwahu fa-saye'a," and its parallel is "sarrartuhu fa-sarra" and "sha'alatuhu fa-sha'ala."

﴿And it will be said﴾: the keepers of Hell will say to them: ﴿This is that which you were calling for﴾, meaning, that He would hasten it for you.

The common reading is ﴿tadda'un﴾ with the doubled dal, of the form "yaftaʻilun" from "du'a'" (calling). According to most scholars, this means they wish for it and seek consolation. Al-Hasan said: it means they claim that there is no paradise and no Fire. Al-Dahhak, Qatada, and Ya'qub read it with a single dal, meaning: you call upon Allah to bring it to you, as in His words: ﴿And when they said: O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [Q 8:32], and so on.

Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Mecca who wish for your destruction and await the calamities of fate: ﴿Have you considered: if Allah destroys me and those with me, or has mercy upon us﴾, meaning He keeps us alive and postpones our terms, ﴿who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?﴾ For it will surely befall them without doubt. This is the view of al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan.

Some said: ﴿Say: Have you considered if Allah destroys me, so He punishes me, and those with me, or has mercy upon us, so He forgives us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?﴾ We, together with our faith, still fear His punishment, because He has the right to seize us for our sins, punish us, and destroy us, since His judgment is just, His command is effective, and His act is realized in His dominion. So even with our faith, we fear His punishment. Who, then, will protect you from the punishment of Allah while you are disbelievers? This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, and the view of Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya and Ibn Kaysan.

﴿Say: He is the Merciful. We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied, so you will know who is in manifest error.﴾ The reading with the ya' ("fa-sayaʻlamun") is by al-Kisa'i, who transmitted it from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). The rest read it with the ta' ("fa-sa-ta'lamun").

﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken (ghawran)?﴾ Meaning: disappearing, vanished, drained into the earth, out of reach of hands and buckets. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: this refers to the water of Zamzam, and the well of Maymun al-Hadrami, which is an ancient well of the 'Ad.

﴿Then who will bring you clear, flowing water?﴾ Apparent, reachable by hands and buckets. 'Ata reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "jar (flowing)." Al-Mu'arrikh said: "sweet, in the dialect of Quraysh."
